1bgvnxn:188: AI applications have two completely different spaces: the Latent space and the Deterministic space. The former is the model's domain—judgment, reading, synthesis, reasoning—capable but uncertain; the latter is code's domain—SQL, compilation, arithmetic, file operations—precise and reproducible. The core mistake is throwing deterministic tasks at the LLM and handing uncertain tasks to humans. A typical counterexample is using an LLM to arrange a seating chart for 800 people; this deterministic scheduling problem makes the model repeatedly agonize over seat conflicts, when code could solve it linearly.
1c646cg:86: : When designing any LLM application workflow, first clarify which space each step belongs to. Judgment, reasoning, generation → LLM; storage, computation, IO, compilation → code. When a mixed zone appears, encapsulate it with a Skill—don't mix.

va2z39:209: : The Latent/Deterministic space separation is not a performance optimization trick but a fundamental architectural judgment. Garry Tan's "Thin Harness, Fat Skills" is essentially saying: decouple the model's fuzzy capabilities (judgment, reasoning, generation) from code's precise capabilities (execution, storage, computation) at the system level.
